changes: Date: the chronogram 'dviṣaṇnagendra' does not give ŚS 1476. Read right to left, dvi=2, ṣaṭ=6, naga=7 and indra (normally 14) gives an impossible 14762. Reading indra as a slip for indu (=1) gives ŚS 1762 (c. 1840 CE). This is the proposed reading and is flagged as uncertain, against the catalogue's 1476.
Date: 'śake 'ṅganāgate 'ruṇe' = in the Śaka year, when the sun (aruṇa) had entered Virgo (aṅganā = Kanyā). Month field set to solar month Kanyā.
Mallinātha: 'Kolamala' is not an institution. It is moved out of affiliation and marked as a corruption of the family name Kolācala.
Notes expanded: unnamed scribe, the verses that follow, and the date conflict.

notes: The scribe is called only 'dvijāgraṇīḥ' (foremost of the twice-born, i.e. a brahmin) and is not named: 'lilekha kāvyapustakaṃ saṭīkakaṃ dvijāgraṇīḥ'. The year is uncertain. The chronogram reads dvi(2)-ṣaṭ(6)-naga(7)-indra. Indra usually stands for 14, which gives an impossible number when read right to left. Taking 'indra' as a slip for 'indu' (1), which fits the pañcacāmara metre equally well, gives ŚS 1762 ≈ 1840 CE, which suits Devanagari on Nepali paper. The catalogue's ŚS 1476 (≈1554 CE) can only be reached by reading indra=14, naga=7, ṣaṭ=6 and dropping dvi, so it looks doubtful. 'aṅganāgate 'ruṇe' means the sun had entered Kanyā (solar month around Bhādra/Āśvina). The verses after the date ('śāstreṣu bhraṣṭā…' and 'malayācalasaṃbhūte…') are stock subhāṣitas, not colophon data. The colophon is for sarga 1 only.
